lesson.menu_desc: A tourist at the bar asks where to eat: giving advice like a local, with should, if I were you, why don't you and you'd better -- 13 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Eat Like a Local
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Eglis Roberto | Lesson 9 -- Eat Like a Local

listenings.text: I have been a waiter in Lisbon for twenty years, and every summer the tourists ask me the same question. Where should we eat? Here is what I tell them. First, if I were you, I would skip every restaurant with a menu in six languages and photos of the food outside. That is a tourist trap. Walk two streets away from the main square, and look for a small place with paper tablecloths and old men watching football. Second, you should order the dish of the day. It is homemade, it is cheap, and it is what the cook ate for lunch. Why don't you try the grilled sardines? In June they are perfect. And one more thing. You had better not ask for a cappuccino after lunch. The waiter will be polite, but he will remember you.

When I travel, I have one simple rule. I eat where the taxi drivers eat. They know the city, they do not have much time, and they do not pay for bad food. So my first advice is this. You should talk to the people who work in the street, not to the hotel. A hotel will always send you somewhere expensive. Second, you could try a street stall for lunch. People are afraid of street food, but if there is a long line of locals, it is usually safe and very good. And if you like spicy food, ask for it the way they eat it, not the tourist version. Honestly, the best meal I have ever had was a bowl of soup on a plastic chair in Hanoi. It cost two dollars, and it was worth every cent.
